name: NGINX
tagline: Event-driven proxy: terminates TLS, routes HTTP, balances TCP and UDP.

howItWorks.title: What it is and where it sits
howItWorks.body:
NGINX is a reverse proxy, web server and load balancer in one event-driven binary.
http mode works at L7: it parses requests and routes on Host, path and headers.
stream mode works at L4: it relays TCP and UDP bytes without parsing them.
TLS terminates at NGINX, so upstream hops can be plain HTTP or re-encrypted.
It sits in the Edge layer, between Users and the Platform.

howItWorks.title: Process model
howItWorks.body:
The master process reads config, binds ports and supervises workers.
Each worker runs a non-blocking event loop and handles thousands of connections.
worker_processes auto starts one worker per CPU core.
Reload starts new workers on the new config and drains the old ones.
Open connections finish on old workers, so a reload drops nothing.

howItWorks.title: HTTP request flow
howItWorks.body:
listen and server_name pick the server block; unmatched requests hit the default server.
location matching order: exact =, then ^~ prefix, then regex in file order, then longest prefix.
proxy_pass forwards to a URL or an upstream pool.
proxy_set_header Host $host passes the original Host to the app.
proxy_http_version 1.1 with an empty Connection header enables upstream keepalive.

howItWorks.title: Configuration model
howItWorks.body:
Config is nested contexts: main, events, http, server, location, plus stream.
Directives inherit downward; a directive set in a child replaces the inherited value.
include splits config into files; keep one file per site in conf.d.
nginx -t validates syntax and referenced files before any reload.
nginx -T dumps the merged effective config for review and support.

howItWorks.title: TLS and security
howItWorks.body:
ssl_certificate and ssl_certificate_key load the chain; restrict ssl_protocols to TLSv1.2 and 1.3.
ssl_session_cache shared:SSL:10m resumes handshakes cheaply across workers.
limit_req and limit_conn throttle abusive clients per key.
allow and deny restrict locations such as status pages to admin networks.
Hide the version with server_tokens off; run workers as an unprivileged user.

howItWorks.title: Load balancing, HA and scaling
howItWorks.body:
upstream pools balance round robin by default; least_conn, hash and random are built in.
Open source health is passive: max_fails and fail_timeout mark a peer down after errors.
Active health checks need NGINX Plus or an external checker.
keepalived VRRP floats one VIP between two NGINX nodes for HA.
Scale out by adding nodes behind a VIP or cloud balancer; keep config identical.

howItWorks.title: Observability
howItWorks.body:
access_log with a custom log_format records upstream time and status per request.
stub_status shows active connections, accepts and requests; bind it to localhost.
nginx-prometheus-exporter converts stub_status into Prometheus metrics.
Alert on 5xx rate, upstream_response_time p95 and dropped connections.
error_log level warn in production; raise to info briefly while debugging.

howItWorks.title: Failure modes and troubleshooting
howItWorks.body:
502 means the upstream refused or reset; 504 means it exceeded proxy_read_timeout.
Check journalctl -u nginx and error.log first, then curl the upstream directly.
Too many open files: raise worker_rlimit_nofile and the systemd LimitNOFILE.
Failed nginx -t keeps the old workers running; fix the file and retry.
A hostname in proxy_pass resolves at startup; use a resolver with a variable for dynamic DNS.

howItWorks.title: Connecting to its neighbours
howItWorks.body:
In front (Users): DNS resolves the name to NGINX, or to a cloud load balancer that forwards to it.
Behind, on VMs (Infrastructure): proxy_pass to app servers; stream relays TCP to databases.
Behind, on Kubernetes (Platform): NodePort opens one port, default 30000 to 32767, on every node; list node IPs as upstreams.
Service type LoadBalancer asks a cloud balancer or MetalLB for one VIP; point NGINX at it.
An Ingress or Gateway API controller routes by Host and path inside the cluster when many apps share one entry.
A ClusterIP is not reachable from outside; never point an external NGINX at it.

howItWorks.title: Alternatives
howItWorks.body:
HAProxy: choose it for deep L4 and L7 load balancing, rich health checks and runtime control.
Envoy: choose it for dynamic xDS config, gRPC and service-mesh use.
Traefik: choose it for automatic discovery of containers and Kubernetes Ingress.
Caddy: choose it for automatic HTTPS and a very short config.
Cloud load balancers: choose them when the provider should run the Edge for you.

flow: Client resolves the name and connects to the address NGINX listens on.
NGINX accepts the connection on a worker and completes the TLS handshake.
server_name and location select the route.
proxy_pass picks a peer from the upstream pool and reuses keepalive.
Peers can be a VM app, a Kubernetes NodePort or a LoadBalancer VIP.
kube-proxy forwards the NodePort connection to a Service endpoint pod.
The stream block relays raw TCP to non-HTTP backends such as PostgreSQL.
access_log and stub_status expose the result.

deploy.summary: Edge VM: hardened host, static address, firewall, NGINX with TLS, a Kubernetes upstream and stream.
prerequisites: Debian or Ubuntu VM with sudo
A DNS name and a static address
Optional Kubernetes nodes exposing a NodePort

steps.title: SSH key and sshd hardening
steps.code:
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "ops@edge"
ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub ops@EDGE_HOST
sudo tee /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-hardening.conf <<'EOF'
PermitRootLogin no
PasswordAuthentication no
KbdInteractiveAuthentication no
AllowUsers ops
EOF
sudo sshd -t && sudo systemctl reload ssh
steps.note: Replace ops and EDGE_HOST. Keep a second session open until key login works.

steps.title: Static address and DNS
steps.code:
# /etc/netplan/01-edge.yaml
network:
  version: 2
  ethernets:
    ens18:
      addresses: [10.0.10.11/24]
      routes:
        - to: default
          via: 10.0.10.1
      nameservers:
        addresses: [10.0.10.2]
steps.note: Replace the interface and addresses, then run sudo netplan apply. Add the A record for example.test.

steps.title: Firewall rules
steps.code:
sudo ufw default deny incoming
sudo ufw allow from ADMIN_CIDR to any port 22 proto tcp
sudo ufw allow 80,443/tcp
sudo ufw allow from APP_CIDR to any port 15432 proto tcp
sudo ufw enable
steps.note: Replace ADMIN_CIDR and APP_CIDR. Backends never face the internet.

steps.title: Install NGINX, stream module and a lab certificate
steps.code:
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y nginx libnginx-mod-stream openssl
sudo mkdir -p /etc/nginx/certs /etc/nginx/stream.d
sudo openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -days 30 -subj "/CN=example.test" \
  -keyout /etc/nginx/certs/tls.key -out /etc/nginx/certs/tls.crt
sudo chmod 600 /etc/nginx/certs/tls.key
steps.note: Lab certificate only; use a real CA or ACME in production. RHEL-family uses dnf install nginx.

steps.title: Write nginx.conf
steps.note: Replaces the packaged file; the modules-enabled include loads the stream module. Keep a backup copy first.

steps.title: Add the TLS server
steps.note: On NGINX 1.25.1 or newer add http2 on; inside the server block.

steps.title: Proxy to a Kubernetes NodePort
steps.note: Replace node IPs and the port from kubectl get svc. List every worker; a dead node is marked down passively.

steps.title: Add the stream L4 proxy and start
steps.note: Later changes: nginx -t, then systemctl reload nginx. Reload drains old workers.

verify: nginx -t reports syntax is ok and test is successful
tail /var/log/nginx/access.log shows upstream address and timing
pitfalls: No proxy_http_version 1.1 and empty Connection means no upstream keepalive.
proxy_set_header in a location replaces every inherited header from the server.
proxy_pass http://app/ versus http://app rewrites the URI differently.
Two proxies in a row each need their own timeouts; the smallest one wins.
A hostname in proxy_pass resolves once at startup; use a resolver and variable.
Open source NGINX has no active health checks; failed requests mark peers down.
Low worker_connections or file limits log 'Too many open files' under load.
keyPoints: One master supervises event-loop workers; reload swaps workers without dropping connections.
The http block routes by Host and path; the stream block proxies TCP and UDP.
TLS terminates at NGINX; upstream pools get health marking, keepalive and balancing.
Test with nginx -t, then reload; roll back by restoring the file.
quickDeploy: Harden SSH, set a static address, open ports.
Write nginx.conf with http, TLS and stream.
Run nginx -t, then start under systemd.
Reload gracefully; watch stub_status and logs.
osiNote: Terminates TLS and routes by Host and path; stream proxies TCP.
production: Set worker_rlimit_nofile and LimitNOFILE; size worker_connections for peak sockets.
Pair two nodes with keepalived VRRP for a floating VIP.
Keep configs in Git; roll back by restoring the file and reloading.
Allow TLSv1.2 and 1.3 only; protect keys with mode 600.
Scrape stub_status; alert on 5xx rate and upstream response time p95.
